overlays.source_span: Obviously, irreducible implies indecomposable, but not vice versa.
overlays.claim: Every irreducible (simple) representation is indecomposable: IsSimpleModule A V → Etingof.IsIndecomposable A V.

overlays.source_span: G/[G, G] \cong \mathbb{F}_q^\times via g \mapsto \det(g). The 1-dimensional representations of G thus have the form \rho(g) = \xi(\det(g)), where \xi is a homomorphism \xi : \mathbb{F}_q^\times \to \mathbb{C}^\times; so there are q - 1 such representations, denoted \mathbb{C}_\xi.
overlays.claim: Every 1-dimensional representation of GL₂(𝔽_q) is of the form g ↦ ξ(det g) for a unique character ξ : 𝔽_q× → ℂ×; there are exactly q−1 such representations.

overlays.source_span: Let G = S_4, H = S_3. Then \operatorname{Ind}_H^G \mathbb{C}_+ = \mathbb{C}_+ \oplus \mathbb{C}^3_-, \operatorname{Ind}_H^G \mathbb{C}_- = \mathbb{C}_- \oplus \mathbb{C}^3_+, \operatorname{Ind}_H^G \mathbb{C}^2 = \mathbb{C}^2 \oplus \mathbb{C}^3_- \oplus \mathbb{C}^3_+.
overlays.claim: The three induced representations of S₄ from S₃: Ind_{S₃}^{S₄} ℂ₊ ≅ ℂ₊ ⊕ ℂ³₋, Ind_{S₃}^{S₄} ℂ₋ ≅ ℂ₋ ⊕ ℂ³₊, Ind_{S₃}^{S₄} ℂ² ≅ ℂ² ⊕ ℂ³₋ ⊕ ℂ³₊

overlays.source_span: Scalar: q-1 (one for every nonzero x); Parabolic: q-1 (one for every nonzero x); Hyperbolic: \frac{1}{2}(q-1)(q-2); Elliptic: \frac{1}{2}q(q-1) [entries in the 'Number of classes' column of the conjugacy class table]
overlays.claim: The number of conjugacy classes of each type in GL₂(𝔽_q): q-1 scalar classes, q-1 parabolic classes, (q-1)(q-2)/2 split-semisimple classes, q(q-1)/2 elliptic classes; totalling q²-1.

overlays.source_span: We have thus found q - 1 1-dimensional representations of G, \frac{q(q-1)}{2} principal series representations, and \frac{q(q-1)}{2} complementary series representations, for a total of q^2 - 1 representations, i.e., the number of conjugacy classes in G. This implies that we have in fact found all i
overlays.claim: The total count (q-1) + q(q-1)/2 + q(q-1)/2 = q²-1 equals the number of conjugacy classes, so the listed representations are all irreducible representations of GL₂(𝔽_q)

overlays.source_span: $\sigma(\rho) \leq \rho$ lexicographically with equality if and only if $\sigma = 1$, and subtracting both sides from the constant vector $\lambda + \rho$ shows that $\lambda + \rho - \sigma(\rho) \geq \lambda$ with equality if and only if $\sigma = 1$.
overlays.claim: For sigma in S_N acting on rho = (N-1, N-2, ..., 0): sigma(rho) <=_lex rho with equality iff sigma = 1; equivalently lambda + rho - sigma(rho) >=_lex lambda with equality iff sigma = 1.

overlays.source_span: It is easy to show that if F is an additive functor, then F(X ⊕ Y) is canonically isomorphic to F(X) ⊕ F(Y).
overlays.claim: An additive functor F between preadditive categories with biproducts satisfies F(X ⊞ Y) ≅ F(X) ⊞ F(Y) canonically.

overlays.source_span: Note that in a semisimple category, any additive functor is automatically exact on both sides.
overlays.claim: For a semisimple abelian category C (every short exact sequence splits), any additive functor F : C → D is both left and right exact.

overlays.source_span: Show that if V is an irreducible complex representation of a finite group G of dimension > 1, then there exists g \in G such that \chi_V(g) = 0.
overlays.claim: For an irreducible complex representation V of a finite group G with dim V > 1, there exists g with χ_V(g) = 0 (Problem 5.2.7 part (b)).
